```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(here)
library(sva)
```

This step removes all unexpressed gene.

```{r}
analysis_tpm <- readRDS("analysis_tpm.rds")

# visualizing dataset
analysis_tpm[, 1:10] %>%
  head(5)

# Creating a vector containing the names of all the gene columns
gene_columns <- 8:ncol(analysis_tpm)

# convert gene columns to numeric
analysis_tpm <- analysis_tpm %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(gene_columns), as.numeric))

# Calculate the total expression for each gene
gene_totals <- colSums(analysis_tpm[, gene_columns],
                       na.rm = TRUE)

# Verify whether there are genes with total count of zero
gene_totals[gene_totals == 0]

expressed_genes <- names(gene_totals[gene_totals > 0])

# Combining expressed genes with demographic characteristics
filtered_analysis_tpm <- analysis_tpm %>%
  select(1:8,all_of(expressed_genes))

# Number of genes before filtering
length(gene_columns) 

# Number of genes after filtering
length(expressed_genes)

```

# PCA analysis

```{r}
# PCA only uses numeric values

pca_data <- filtered_analysis_tpm %>%
  select(all_of(expressed_genes))

# Using the normalized (TPM) values 
## Expected to do the same with the TMM values
pca_tpm <- prcomp(pca_data, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# The proportion of variability explained by each PC
pc_plot_data <- data.frame(
  PC = 1:ncol(pca_tpm$x),
  Variance = summary(pca_tpm)$importance["Proportion of Variance", ] * 100)

pca_plot <- ggplot(pc_plot_data, aes(x = PC, y = Variance)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "PCA Plot",
    x = "Principal Component",
    y = "Percentage of Variance Explained"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(here("output", "pca_plot.png"), pca_plot, width = 8, height = 6)
pca_plot

```

Will be using PC1 and PC2 for the inital visaulization

## Exploring PCA by available demographics characteristics

```{r}
## SEX
pca_scores$biological_sex <- filtered_analysis_tpm$biological_sex

pca_sex_plot <- ggplot(pca_scores, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = biological_sex)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA by Sex",
    x = "PC1",
    y = "PC2",
    color = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(here("output", "pca_sex_plot.png"), pca_sex_plot, width = 8, height = 6)
pca_sex_plot
```

```{r}
## AGE GROUP
# Categorizing based on the median, Q1 and Q3 (No research)

filtered_analysis_tpm <- filtered_analysis_tpm %>%
  mutate(Age_group = case_when(
    age < 53 ~ "Under 53",
    age >= 53 & age <= 65 ~ "53-65",
    age >= 65 & age <= 72 ~ "65-72",
    age >= 72 ~ "72+"
  ))

pca_scores$Age_group <- filtered_analysis_tpm$Age_group

pca_age_cat_plot <- ggplot(pca_scores, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Age_group)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA by Age Group",
    x = "PC1",
    y = "PC2",
    color = "Age_group"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  ## this part of the code removes the two extreme values to zoom in on the rest of the participants
  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(-50, 50),
    ylim = c(-100, 60)
  )

ggsave(here("output", "pca_age_cat_plot.png"), pca_age_cat_plot, width = 8, height = 6)
pca_age_cat_plot
```

```{r}
## Age as continuous

pca_age_cont_plot
```

```{r}
## number of prior vaccination

filtered_analysis_tpm <- filtered_analysis_tpm %>%
  mutate(vaccines = case_when(
    n_prior_vax ==0  ~ "Unknown",
    n_prior_vax >= 0 & n_prior_vax <= 5 ~ "<5",
    n_prior_vax >= 5 & n_prior_vax <= 10 ~ "5-10",

    x = "PC1",
    y = "PC2",
    color = "Vaccines number"

  theme_minimal() + 
  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(-50, 50),

ggsave(here("output", "pca_vax_cat_plot.png"), pca_vax_cat_plot, width = 8, height = 6)
pca_vax_cat_plot
```

```{r}
## number of prior vaccination (as continuous)

# Create a separate variable for PCA
filtered_analysis_tpm <- filtered_analysis_tpm %>%
  mutate(n_prior_vax_pca = na_if(n_prior_vax, 0))

# Add continuous vaccination variable to PCA scores
pca_scores$n_prior_vax <- filtered_analysis_tpm$n_prior_vax_pca

pca_vax_plot_b <- ggplot(pca_scores, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = n_prior_vax )) +
  geom_point(size = 3,  alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_gradient(
    low = "green",
    high = "red",
    na.value = "grey",
    breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 4),
    labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 1),
    name = "Number of previous vaccines"
    )+
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-50, 50), ylim = c(-100, 60)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "PCA by Previous Vaccination",
    x = "PC1",
    y = "PC2"
  )

ggsave(here("output", "pca_vax_plot_b.png"), pca_vax_plot_b, width = 8, height = 6)
pca_vax_plot_b
```


```{r}
pca_scores$plasmablast_frequency <- filtered_analysis_tpm$plasmablast_frequency

pca_plasm_plot <- ggplot(pca_scores, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = plasmablast_frequency)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_gradient(
    low = "green",
    high = "red",
    name = "Day 7 Plasmablast frequency"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-50, 50), ylim = c(-100, 60)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "PCA of baseline gene expression",
    x = "PC1",
    y = "PC2"
  )

ggsave(here("output", "pca_plasm_plot.png"), pca_plasm_plot, width = 8, height = 6)
pca_plasm_plot

```

Most participants clustered relatively close together on all variables. 
- Participants with higher plasmablast frequencies did not form an obvious separate cluster. There was no obvious gradient in plasmablast frequency across PC1 and PC2.
- participants with higher number of previosu vaccination did form a gradient across PC1 and PC2. 

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Further analysis

```{r}
## investigate PC association with Day 7 plasmablast frequency

cor.test(
  pca_scores$PC1,
  pca_scores$plasmablast_frequency,
  method = "spearman",
  use = "complete.obs"
)

# PC2 correlation
cor.test(
  pca_scores$PC2,
  pca_scores$plasmablast_frequency,
  method = "spearman",
  use = "complete.obs"
)
```

## PCA loadings

Which genes contribute most to overall variation?
  
```{r}
## Genes contributing most to PC1 and PC2
## Can be used for enrichment (with DAVID)

loadings <- as.data.frame(pca_tpm$rotation)
loadings$Gene_ID <- rownames(loadings)

top_PC1 <- loadings %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(PC1))) %>%
  select(PC1) %>%
  head(10)

top_PC1


top_PC2 <- loadings %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(PC2))) %>%
  select(PC2) %>%
  head(10)

top_PC2
```
